idiom_name: switch pattern matching with record patterns and sealed interfaces
implementation_notes: Java 21 makes pattern matching for switch final: type patterns, record patterns, guarded patterns (when) and case null, with coverage checked by the compiler against the permits clause of a sealed interface. The check is real - a switch expression must cover every permitted subtype or it does not compile - so omit default in the normal case and keep the compiler in charge. At run time an exhaustive pattern switch can still throw MatchException when the sealed hierarchy changed after the switch was compiled, so recompile the switch whenever permits changes; that stale-artefact path is the price of following the compiler rather than a catch-all.
pitfalls: Guarded cases never count as coverage, so a case Circle c when c.r() > 0 still leaves other Circle values unhandled and another arm is required.
A switch compiled against an older sealed hierarchy throws MatchException at run time when a new permitted subtype appears; recompile the class holding the switch.
Type erasure prevents matching parameterised types such as List<String>; only the raw type can be tested, and dominated cases are rejected at compile time.

variants.name: Java 17 sealed hierarchy with an instanceof pattern chain
variants.idiom_name: instanceof type patterns in an if/else chain over a sealed interface
variants.implementation_notes: On Java 17 the pattern switch exists only as a preview, so a production codebase models the closed set as a sealed interface (permanent in 17, JEP 409) and dispatches with an if/else chain of instanceof patterns (permanent in 16, JEP 394), ending in an else branch that throws for the impossible case. Coverage is no longer proved by the compiler: the chain is open by construction, so the final else is a runtime fail-fast rather than a proof, and every added permitted subtype is a fall-through risk. Switch expressions over enums (Java 14) do keep compiler-checked exhaustiveness for enum constants, so use them where the variant set is an enum and rebuild the type-pattern chain as a total match as soon as the toolchain moves to 21.
pitfalls: The chain is exhaustive only by convention: a newly permitted subtype compiles everywhere and reaches the runtime throw instead of breaking the build.
Order matters: a broader instanceof test placed before a narrower one makes the later branch unreachable, and only IDE analysis flags it.
